## Findings

1. **F1 — Dependency completion is falsely documented as automatically promoting dependents to `ready`.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:229) and [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:776) call `Backlog → Ready` an automatic transition. [quickstart.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/quickstart.md:124), [first-workflow.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/first-workflow.md:177), and [adopt-planning-bracket.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/adopt-planning-bracket.md:314) rely on the same behavior. In current source, completing or rejecting a dependency does not scan and promote its dependents: `query available` still excludes the persisted `backlog` issue. Promotion occurs through an explicit ready update, `jit validate --fix`, or the dependency-removal path. Remediate the lifecycle reference and walkthroughs with one of those actual promotion operations.

2. **F2 — The quickstart claims a lifecycle path its commands do not follow.** [quickstart.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/quickstart.md:12) and [quickstart.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/quickstart.md:170) say the tutorial follows `backlog → ready → in_progress → done`. Dependency-free issues are created in `ready`, and the tutorial completes or gates them without entering `in_progress`; only one issue temporarily enters `backlog` after adding a dependency. Remediate these summaries to describe the states the walkthrough actually exercises, or add the missing explicit transitions.

3. **F3 — Dependency examples incorrectly require `done` rather than either terminal outcome.** [core-model.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/concepts/core-model.md:435), [first-workflow.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/tutorials/first-workflow.md:143), and [research-projects.md](/home/vkaskivuo/Projects/just-in-time/docs/how-to/research-projects.md:121) say dependencies wait for work to be done. `State::is_terminal` treats both `done` and `rejected` as satisfying dependencies. Remediate the examples to say “reaches a terminal state (`done` or `rejected`)”; use a validation rule or gate if the workflow specifically requires successful completion.

Total findings: 3
